title: Two misreadings of the three eunuchs
english: On the difference among eunuchs. “For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb,” up to “Let the one who is able to receive this receive it” (Matthew 19:12). Before giving the interpretation of this passage that appears true to us, I will set out two misinterpretations that are going to arise about this text, and then refute them as far as I am able, so that by guarding against every error in what will be said, we may grasp the true meaning and so come to the matter at hand.

Some people, thinking that the third kind of eunuch is bodily just as the two bodily eunuchisms they saw were, dared to offer themselves to a eunuchism of the same kind as the first two—out of fear of God, but without understanding—and they have subjected themselves to reproach and perhaps even to shame, and not only among those outside the faith alone.

Others, not many, have taken the first two kinds as spoken by the Savior in a straightforward bodily sense, but they have understood the third no longer according to the letter, but as the eunuchism that comes from reason, when by purpose for the kingdom of heaven they have cut out the desiring part with the most cutting reason and have despised the outrages of the body.

title: The letter kills: two readings of the three eunuchisms
english: We must understand that the earlier friends of the gospel's letter, who did not notice that Jesus spoke these things in parables and that they were said by the Spirit, leveled out the third kind to match the first two. For if the two are spoken bodily, it follows that the third is bodily as well. The second group applied to the third kind a sound interpretation, thinking that the cutting out of the passionate part from the soul by reason is what is meant, but they no longer saw that it was fitting to take the first two allegorically as well. And if it is possible to say in other places, "The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life" (2 Corinthians 3:6), the same must be said here: the kept line about the two eunuchisms killed those who understood the third in the same way. If anyone wants to show from other examples that the New Testament has a letter that kills, let him hear how the Savior says to the apostles: "When I sent you out without a purse, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?" (Luke 22:35) Then he says, "Now let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag, and let the one who has none sell his cloak and buy a sword" (Luke 22:36). For the one who does not understand and buys a murderous sword will perish against the will of Jesus, having taken the word badly. Glory to Christ. Amen.
